Take Ownership of Modern DevSecOps Environments Across Secure and Mission-Critical Systems   Your new company     
 Our client is a leading organisation operating within a secure and technically complex environment and is seeking to engage a DevSecOps Engineer on a permanent basis. Working as part of a collaborative engineering team, you will contribute to the delivery and sustainment of modern software development platforms, automation capabilities and secure infrastructure that support critical business outcomes.   This role is based in Brisbane and requires a commitment to working onsite 4-5 days per week. Due to the nature of the environment, this position cannot be performed remotely. Brisbane-based candidates are strongly preferred, however applications are welcomed from interstate candidates who are genuinely committed to relocating. Joining a collaborative engineering team, you will contribute to the delivery and sustainment of modern software development platforms, automation capabilities and secure infrastructure supporting critical business outcomes.  An NV2 Security Clearance is highly desirable. We also encourage applications from candidates who hold NV1 or Baseline clearances, or Australian Citizens who are eligible and willing to obtain a security clearance. 
   Your new role     
 As a DevSecOps Engineer, you will play a key role in the design, implementation and ongoing support of secure software development environments and CI/CD pipelines. Working alongside engineering, infrastructure and security teams, you will help drive automation, improve platform performance and ensure development environments remain secure, scalable and compliant.   
  Key responsibilities:   
 
 Designing, implementing and maintaining secure CI/CD pipelines 
 Supporting and optimising secure software development environments 
 Deploying, configuring and maintaining Kubernetes and Docker platforms 
 Developing and supporting GitLab CI/CD workflows and integrations 
 Managing Linux and Windows-based development environments 
 Building and maintaining Ansible automation and configuration management solutions 
 Troubleshooting platform, infrastructure and application issues 
 Producing and maintaining technical documentation and configuration records 
 Supporting ongoing platform maintenance, upgrades and continuous improvement activities 
 
  What you'll need to succeed     
 To be successful, you will bring proven experience within DevSecOps, platform engineering or infrastructure automation environments, along with a strong focus on security, reliability and operational excellence. 
   
  Key requirements:  
 
 CI/CD pipeline design, implementation and support 
 GitLab administration and pipeline development 
 Kubernetes and Docker environments 
 Ansible and Infrastructure as Code methodologies 
 Linux administration, particularly Ubuntu and Red Hat 
 Secure software development environments and DevSecOps practices 
 Technical troubleshooting and performance optimisation 
 Documentation, change management and governance processes 
 
  Highly desirable:  
 
 Defence, government or other highly regulated environments 
 Security governance and compliance frameworks 
 Certifications such as Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA), RHCSA or similar 
 Tertiary qualifications in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cyber Security or a related discipline 
 
  What you'll get in return     
 
 Exposure to modern DevSecOps, automation and cloud-native technologies 
 The opportunity to work within a secure and technically advanced environment 
 A collaborative team culture that values innovation, continuous improvement and technical excellence 
 Long-term career development and professional growth opportunities 
 
  What you need to do now     If you're interested in this role, click 'apply now' to forward an up-to-date copy of your CV, or call us now.   If this job isn't quite right for you, but you are looking for a new position, please contact us for a confidential discussion on your career.    Please  click here  to apply.

result.description: Mansys Pty Ltd   Electrical Engineering Technician    Employer:  Integra Switchboards Pty Ltd   Location:  Brendale, Queensland 4500   Position:  Full-time   Salary:  AUD 80,000 to A$90,000 per annum plus superannuation, commensurate with skills and experience       Integra Switchboards Pty Ltd is seeking a skilled and experienced Electrical Engineering Technician to join their team in Brendale, Queensland. The successful candidate will support the design, manufacture, testing, commissioning and quality checking of low-voltage electrical switchboards, distribution boards, motor control centres and control panels.  This role is suited to a technically competent person with experience in electrical systems, switchboard manufacture, testing procedures, technical drawings, electrical components and Australian electrical standards.   Key duties and responsibilities   The Electrical Engineering Technician will be responsible for:   Assisting Electrical Engineers, project managers and senior technical staff with the design and layout of electrical switchboards, distribution boards, motor control centres, control panels, cabling arrangements and associated electrical systems.  Preparing, interpreting and reviewing technical drawings, wiring diagrams, layout drawings, schematics and electrical plans for switchboard manufacturing projects.  Conducting tests on electrical systems, components and switchboard assemblies to confirm operational performance, safety and compliance with project specifications.  Collecting technical data, recording test results, performing calculations, preparing test documentation, charts, reports and tabulations for engineering and quality assurance purposes.  Assisting with estimating material requirements, component quantities, labour requirements and project costs for switchboard and electrical assembly works.  Inspecting designs, manufactured switchboards and completed electrical assemblies to ensure compliance with specifications, Australian Standards, client requirements and safety requirements.  Assembling, installing, testing, calibrating, modifying and repairing electrical equipment, switchboard components, protection devices, metering equipment, indicating devices and control equipment.  Supporting workshop electrical functions, including installation of assemblies for protection relays, metering devices, control circuits and electrical indicating equipment.  Assisting with fault finding, technical problem solving and rectification of electrical issues during manufacture, testing and commissioning.  Liaising with internal design, fabrication, assembly and project teams to ensure switchboards are delivered accurately, safely and on time.  Maintaining accurate technical records, testing records, compliance documents and quality assurance documentation.  Ensuring all work is performed in accordance with workplace health and safety requirements, company procedures, project specifications and relevant Australian Standards.    Skills and experience required   Applicants must have:   Diploma or Bachelors in Electrical Engineering or related field  Atleast 2 years of experience in electrical switchboard manufacture, electrical systems, control panels, distribution boards, motor control centres or similar electrical engineering environments.  Ability to read and interpret electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, schematics and technical specifications.  Experience conducting electrical tests, recording results and assisting with technical reporting.  Knowledge of electrical components such as circuit breakers, busbars, contactors, relays, metering equipment, control devices, terminals and cabling systems.    Skills Required    Good technical problem-solving skills and strong attention to detail.  Ability to work safely and effectively in a workshop/manufacturing environment.  Good communication skills and ability to work as part of a technical project team.      Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We are seeking a highly skilled Electronic Equipment Trades Worker to join our technical operations team.  You will perform highly skilled technical duties involving installation, advanced fault diagnosing, testing, repairing, servicing, precise calibration of complex and a wide range of electronic equipment and household electrical appliances including televisions, audiovisual equipment, display devices, home entertainment systems, security cameras, microwave ovens, refrigerators, washing machines, coffee machines, air fryer and other electronic products. You will ensure that all technical opearations adhere stricly to Australian Standards and corporate regulatory frameworks.   Benefits   Opportunities to grow and develop internally within the company  Competitive Salary  Friendly and collaborative work environment                Task & responsibilities   Diagnose faults and perform testing on machines, instruments, electronics and electrical products, audiovisual equipment, control system, household appliances and other consumer electronic products.  Repair electronic and electrical equipment by replacing worn and defective components, carrying out component-level repairs and performing soldering.  Reassemble, calibrate and perform thoroughly test and adjust equipment to ensure safe and reliable operation.  Service televisions, home entertainment systems, display equipment, personal computers, microwave ovens, coffee machines, air fryers, vacuum cleaners, refrigerators, washing machines, air conditioners and other consumer electronics.  Install, replace and configure electronic instruments and control systems including control boards, sensors.   Apply knowledge of electrical, electronic, hydraulic, mechanical and pneumatic principles to diagnose faults, perform maintenance, troubleshoot issues and repair a wide range of electronic equipment, control system and electrical appliances.  Interpret diagnostic error codes and communicate technical information clearly.  Provide users with clear guidance on correct operating procedures to help prevent future malfunctions.    Qualification & experience   Relevant qualification or trade certification in electronics, electrical engineering, or a related field.  At least 1 year of experience as an Electronic Equipment Trades Worker or in a similar role.  Demonstrated experience diagnosing, testing, repairing, and servicing consumer electronics, audiovisual equipment, and household electrical appliances.  Strong component-level fault-finding and repair skills, including soldering and replacement of electronic components.  Sound knowledge of electrical and electronic systems and diagnostic techniques. From humble beginnings in 1990 from a small country Bakery, to 36 years later, known in the region for our quality artisan products, cafe menu and the best beverages in town.

Qualifications, skills and experience are essential.

Continuous Learning and Safety We believe in the power of ongoing learning and development. That's why we provide comprehensive training to ensure you excel in your role. Safety is our top priority, and you'll be expected to comply with all company Policies and Procedures.

We are a wholly Australian owned company based in Canberra and was first established in 1980.
